sections.h2: Where is Anne Arundel County, Maryland, and what is it like?
sections.html:
Anne Arundel County lies south of Baltimore on the western shore of the Chesapeake Bay, and its county seat is Annapolis, which is also the state capital. The county covers 588 square miles, but 173 of them (29 percent) are water, so shoreline and tidal creeks shape much of the housing stock.

Most of the county's borders are water. The Chesapeake Bay is to the east, the Patuxent River forms the western line with Prince George's County, and the Patapsco River forms the northern line with Baltimore County. The Magothy, Severn, South and West rivers flow into the bay from north to south. Almost all of the county sits on the Atlantic Coastal Plain, with elevation running from sea level to roughly 300 feet near the fall line.

The county was founded on April 9, 1650, and named for Lady Anne Arundell, wife of Cecilius Calvert, the second Baron Baltimore. The 2020 census counted 588,261 residents. Glen Burnie is the largest community, and others include Severna Park, Pasadena, Odenton, Crofton, Arnold, Linthicum, Severn, Gambrills, Davidsonville, Deale and Jessup.

sections.h2: What drives the Anne Arundel County economy and housing demand?
sections.html:
Anne Arundel's economy leans on federal work, defense contractors, an international airport and the state capital. A November 2014 employer list compiled on Wikipedia put Fort George G. Meade, including the National Security Agency, at 53,733 employees, with Northrop Grumman at 7,725, Anne Arundel Health System at 4,000, Southwest Airlines at 3,200 and Maryland Live! Casino at 3,000. Those are dated figures, so treat them as a snapshot of the largest employers rather than current headcounts.

The U.S. Naval Academy and St. John's College are both in Annapolis, and Anne Arundel Community College has several locations. Anne Arundel County Public Schools covers the entire county, so there is one district name on every address. Baltimore-Washington International Thurgood Marshall Airport, the MTA light rail's northern portion and MARC commuter service at BWI give commuters options toward Baltimore and Washington.

County government has operated under a charter since 1965, with a county executive and a seven-member county council.

sections.h2: How was Anne Arundel County reassessed most recently?
sections.html:
Maryland's Department of Assessments and Taxation (SDAT) reassessed Anne Arundel County for January 1, 2026, with notices mailed on December 30, 2025. The state's report on that group shows how much value moved over the three years since the last look.

Measure (Jan. 1, 2023 to Jan. 1, 2026)Anne Arundel County
Combined full cash value$46.52 billion to $53.53 billion (up 15.1%)
Residential value$31.23 billion to $36.24 billion (up 16.0%)
Commercial value$15.28 billion to $17.29 billion (up 13.1%)
Residential properties that rose in value98.98%

Any increase is phased in evenly over three years, while a decrease takes full effect in the 2026 tax year. An owner can appeal within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. Appeals start with SDAT, then go to the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board, then the Maryland Tax Court. The homestead credit limits yearly growth in taxable assessment on a principal residence, with a state cap of 10 percent and lower limits set by some local governments.

sections.h2: When are Anne Arundel County property tax bills due?
sections.html:
Anne Arundel property tax bills are mailed in July to the address on file with SDAT, and the tax is due without interest as of July 1, with a September 30 deadline. Owners of a principal residence can split the bill into two installments, due September 30 and December 31.

The county's fiscal year 2027 page, covering July 1, 2026 to June 30, 2027, adds a 0.87 percent service charge on the balance of the second installment. State law lets local governments add up to 1.65 percent, so the county's charge is below the ceiling. Paying the full bill by September 30 avoids the charge.

  • State rate: $0.112 per $100 of taxable assessment.
  • City of Annapolis rate: $0.738 per $100, which applies to addresses inside the city.
  • Escrowed owners who want to pay annually should notify their lender by May 1.
  • Homestead credit applications are due December 31 to take effect from July 1 of the following year.

The county rate shown on the county's pages is inconsistent between two views, so check the current rate table for your address with the office before you estimate a bill.

sections.h2: Which offices help with an Anne Arundel County property tax question?
sections.html:
The Real Property Tax Division at 44 Calvert Street, Room 110, Annapolis, answers billing questions, and SDAT handles values and ownership records. The division is open Monday through Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., its phone is (410) 222-1736, and its email is realproperty@aacounty.org.

Other useful numbers for a seller:

  • Finance Department customer service: (410) 222-1144.
  • Land Records, for deeds and liens: (410) 222-1425.
  • SDAT, for ownership and mailing address changes: (410) 974-5709.
  • Cashier's offices, including Glen Burnie: Monday through Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m., effective November 2, 2026. After hours, sealed check payments can go in the yellow drop-off box and are processed the next business day.

If you paid a bill for a property you no longer own, the county asks you to contact the office about a possible refund. Credit balances from adjusted bills are refunded as soon as possible.

sections.h2: What transfer and recordation taxes apply to a sale in Anne Arundel County?
sections.html:
A deed in Anne Arundel County carries a county recordation tax of $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the nearest $500, and a county transfer tax of 1.0 percent up to $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent at $1 million or more. The county's Recordation and Transfer Tax Division collects them, and every instrument that might be subject to these taxes must be endorsed by that office before it is recorded.

Checks are payable to Anne Arundel County. State transfer tax and recording fees are handled by the Anne Arundel County Land Records Office at (410) 222-1425, and e-recording is available for land records. The county also posts claim-for-refund forms for both taxes and an affidavit form for certain transactions.

These pages do not say which side of a sale customarily pays each tax. That is set in the sales contract, so your title company should itemize it before you accept an offer.

sections.h2: What should waterfront sellers in Anne Arundel County know about the Critical Area?
sections.html:
The Critical Area is the land and water within 1,000 feet of tidal waters, and in Anne Arundel County it can change what a buyer may do with a lot.

  • The Critical Area Buffer extends 100 feet landward from tidal waters, tributary stream banks and tidal wetland boundaries, and disturbing it generally requires an approved variance.
  • Removing any tree or vegetation, including dead trees, requires an approved Vegetation Management Plan.
  • Grading disturbances over 5,000 square feet need a grading permit.
  • In limited development and resource conservation areas, impervious surface is capped at 15 to 31 percent of the site.

The county's Critical Area Planner of the Day is at the Heritage Complex, 2664 Riva Road, Annapolis, at (410) 222-7960. A seller with a pier, deck or bulkhead near the water should gather any permits on file before listing. The county's page does not describe any notice rule for sellers, so confirm that point with your title company.

sections.h2: What happens if Anne Arundel County taxes are not paid?
sections.html:
Unpaid Maryland property tax becomes a lien that the county can sell at a tax sale, and Anne Arundel holds its sale in June on a date set by the Controller. The State Tax Sale Ombudsman explains that the owner keeps the property after the sale, but the buyer receives a tax lien certificate and the right to foreclose if the debt stays unpaid.

Before the sale, the collector must mail notice to the owner at least 30 days before the property is first advertised, and the advertisement runs weekly for four weeks. A buyer may file a foreclosure complaint six months after the sale, or nine months for an owner-occupied home, and the certificate becomes void if no foreclosure action follows within two years. The ombudsman's page lists redemption interest of 1.5 percent per month for Anne Arundel, so waiting raises the payoff.

Limited-income, elderly and disabled homeowners may qualify for help through the state's Homeowner Protection Program, and the ombudsman will meet by appointment at 123 Market Place, Baltimore.

faqs.q: When are Anne Arundel County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Taxes are due without interest as of July 1 and must be paid by September 30. Principal residences can pay half by September 30 and the balance by December 31.

faqs.q: What is the semiannual service charge in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: The county's fiscal year 2027 page lists a 0.87 percent charge on the balance of the second installment. Paying the full amount by September 30 avoids it.

faqs.q: How do I appeal an Anne Arundel County assessment?
faqs.a: File with SDAT within 45 days of the Notice of Assessment. If you disagree with the result, the next steps are the county's Property Tax Assessment Appeals Board and then the Maryland Tax Court.

faqs.q: What are the transfer tax rates in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: The county transfer tax is 1.0 percent for transactions up to $999,999.99 and 1.5 percent for $1 million or more. The recordation tax is $7.00 per thousand, rounded up to the nearest $500.

faqs.q: Does the Critical Area affect selling a house near the water in Anne Arundel County?
faqs.a: It can. Land within 1,000 feet of tidal waters is in the Critical Area, which has a 100 foot buffer, vegetation plan rules and grading permit thresholds that a buyer may need to understand.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Anne Arundel County house that is behind on taxes?
faqs.a: Yes, but the balance must be handled at or before closing. Call the Real Property Tax Division at (410) 222-1736 for the amount owed, and act before the June tax sale.
